About the Publication

Why The Disclosure exists

India's ESG discourse tends to happen at altitude — in policy documents, investor frameworks, and compliance checklists. The Disclosure brings it to ground level: specific cases, specific legal questions, specific gaps between what the law requires and what actually happens.

Each brief is structured the same way a legal memo is — facts, applicable framework, analysis, recommendations. The goal is not commentary. It is analysis that practitioners, students, and anyone who reads the fine print can use.

The Disclosure is founded and edited by Aily Sadwika, a second-year LLB (Hons.) student at the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, with a prior Master's in Health Psychology from the University of Hyderabad. Her work spans environmental compliance research with the Human Rights Forum (AP & Telangana), ADR and mediation at YCM Conflict Management, and field-based welfare research on urban informal labour. She presented on whistleblower protection frameworks for ESG concerns at NLIU Bhopal's national conference on the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (October 2025).

This publication exists because the cases worth analysing are rarely the ones making headlines — and because the law, read carefully, almost always has more to say than the headlines suggest.
